messages:
eva: Nightly eval job failed, seeing repeated metric regressions for rouge/accuracy on quantized-7b variant. Suspect eval-runner change from yesterday.

ci-bot: Job eval/eval-runner-nightly (build 4821) FAILED
- exit code 1
- failure: AssertionError: metric mismatch > 2.0

jonah: Can you paste the failing assertion stacktrace?

maria: here's the excerpt from logs:
```
AssertionError: mean_delta(metric='rougeL', base=0.842, new=0.798) > 0.02
  File /srv/eval/runner/compare.py, line 214, in compare
    assert abs(delta) <= threshold
```

sam: hmm, yesterday I merged the 'runner-timeout-optim' PR (PR #2198) that touches cache eviction and batching. Could be related.

jonah: bisect suggestion: revert that PR in CI and re-run nightly. Anyone object? :thinking:

eva: do it. we can't ship RC while evals are unstable.

lucy: I'm queueing a revert patch: cherry-pick revert of PR #2198 into branch release/1.4.1 and triggering eval-nightly.

ci-bot: Started job eval/eval-runner-nightly (build 4822) with commit revert-pr-2198

... and after some time ...

ci-bot: Job eval/eval-runner-nightly (build 4822) SUCCESS

eva: OK that's a clear bisect signal. PR #2198 introduced regression.

maria: Root cause quick note: the PR changed how the runner reuses KV cache across short-lived sessions; under heavy parallelism a cache eviction race produced slightly different tokenization ordering which impacted deterministic metrics.

sam: I can send a follow-up PR to make eviction atomic and add a unit test. I'll also add a canary eval job that runs quantized variants overnight.

jonah: For release decision: revert merged into release branch -> good. For mainline: block PR #2198 until fix + test + perf baseline. Also add regression monitor alert on rougeL delta > 1.5%.

eva: Agreed. Also add an annotation in release notes about temporary revert and that baseline numbers were unstable.

maria: I'll open a small benchmark PR showing perf cost of atomic eviction (<1% latency impact). Assign to Sam.

sam: on it. ETA EOD tomorrow.

eva: Great. Thanks everyone. Closing thread when follow-up PRs land.
